question: to the Commission Elena Kountoura (The Left) Subject:

According to recent statements by the CEO of Hellenic Railways1, the European signalling and automatic braking system (ETCS) is still not fully operational on the Greek railway network three and a half years after the criminal railway disaster at Tempi, despite repeated commitments by the Greek Government2. At the same time, according to railway sector representatives, there are still signalling ‘dead spots’ and significant delays in completing critical infrastructure projects, making it impossible to keep to the given timeline3. What is more, the Regulatory Authority for Railways (RAS) has found that a significant number of Hellenic Train vehicles do not meet the requirements for the proper functioning of the ETCS4. These developments raise serious questions as to the respect of the timeline set out in the action plan submitted by the Greek Government to the Commission, as well as the effectiveness of the ongoing infringement procedure for the protection of passengers on the Greek railway network. With this in mind, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What view does it take of the fact that, three and a half years after the Tempi accident, the ETCS is still not fully operational on the Greek railway network, despite the obligations under EU law?
When should the ETCS be fully operational in line with the action plan?

What measures does it intend to take in the context of the infringement procedure, given that the full operation of the ETCS is still delayed, despite repeated commitments by the Greek Government, undermining the safety of passengers?

On 23 July, the CEO of Hellenic Railways stated before the competent parliamentary committee that ‘the ETCS is not currently operational’, while Hellenic Railways clarified that its operation would only start once the certification and licensing procedures had been completed. 2 The Prime Minister had promised that the ETCS would be operational by November 2025, after which the Deputy Transport Minister announced that the Athens-Thessaloniki line would have fully operational safety systems by the end of August 2026. 3 According to the head of the OSE workers’ union, ‘... there is no prospect of the infrastructure projects being completed within the next six months. It is therefore difficult to make electronic safety systems fully operational as well’. 4 The RAS has identified that 100 vehicles (approximately 70 trains) belonging to Hellenic Train do not meet the European technical specifications for the proper functioning of the ETCS, with dozens lacking documentation. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.9.2026) The Commission is aware of the difficulties faced by Greece with the European Rail Traffic Management System (ERTMS) deployment, which are common in many Member States. Given the complexity of this process, the European Union Agency for Railways, at the request of Greece, is supporting the Greek stakeholders in developing an effective ERTMS deployment plan taking into account the applicable deadlines set out in the revised trans-European transport network (TEN-T) Regulation1. Greece is currently preparing the above-mentioned ERTMS deployment plan which will be formally notified to the Commission in the coming months. The plan is expected to include dates by which ERTMS will be put into operation on specific lines. The infringement proceeding case INFR (2023)20362 concerns failure to comply with the requirements of the Rail Safety Directive3. The deployment of European Train Control System (ETCS), key part of ERTMS, is not in the scope of this proceeding. The Commission also notes that although deployment of ETCS on the network contributes to the improvement of rail safety, it is possible for the railway system to operate safely without it, provided that appropriate alternative risk control measures are implemented.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 on Union

guidelines for the development of the trans-European transport network, amending Regulations (EU) 2021/1153 and (EU) No 913/2010 and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1315/2013, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1679/oj. 2 Press release: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/inf_24_6006. 3 Directive (EU) 2016/798 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2016 on railway safety (recast), ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2016/798/oj.
